kept.title: `react/no-danger` set to "warn" contradicts stated intent
kept.desc: The block's comment says these rules "fail loudly if a future change tries to weaken any of those", but `react/no-danger` is only a warning, so introducing `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` will not fail `npm run lint`/CI unless lint runs with `--max-warnings=0`; either set it to "error" or fix the comment.

kept.title: `trust: true` selector is trivially bypassed
kept.desc: `Property[key.name='trust'][value.value=true]` only matches an identifier key with a literal `true`, so `{ "trust": true }`, `{ trust: !!1 }`, `{ trust: () => true }`, or `trust` supplied via a variable/spread all slip through, which undercuts the comment claiming the selector is "broad enough" to be a reliable guardrail.

kept.title: rehype-raw restriction misses subpaths and non-static imports
kept.desc: `paths: [{ name: "rehype-raw" }]` does not match `rehype-raw/lib/...`, `require("rehype-raw")`, or dynamic `import()`; adding a `patterns: ["rehype-raw", "rehype-raw/*"]` entry would close the obvious gaps.

kept.title: `npm audit` makes CI non-deterministic and duplicated
kept.desc: The step hits the registry on every push/PR (and runs twice, once per Node matrix entry), so a newly published high-severity advisory in a prod dep breaks unrelated branches — the exact failure mode the comment claims to avoid by using `--audit-level=high`.
